whatItIs.text: The 'warm spices' blend of the Indian subcontinent — cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, peppercorns, cumin and more, roasted then ground; every region and family keeps its own ratio.

historyNote.text: Garam masala is the parent of Britain's curry powder, which was adapted from it for Western markets; within India none of its many regional recipes is considered more authentic than another.

howToChoose.text: Buy small quantities of freshly ground, or better, grind your own from whole toasted spices; the blend should smell sweetly pungent, not flat.

storage.text: Keep in an airtight tin away from heat and light; it fades within months.

useItUp.text: Sprinkle it at the end of cooking, when its aromatics matter most — over dals, roast cauliflower, or scrambled eggs; a pinch wakes up tomato soup too.

substitutions.note: sharper and turmeric-forward; different character but works
